concepts.caption: One Bitcoin is 100,000,000 sats. Thinking in sats makes it easier to picture buying a fraction of a coin. No price talk, just the unit people end up using once they start stacking.

concepts.caption: 1 Bitcoin is 100,000,000 sats. That is the full unit broken into pieces small enough for everyday buying, including the smallest DCA purchase. No price mentioned, just the math behind every Bitcoin transaction.

concepts.caption: Mt. Gox, QuadrigaCX, FTX, Celsius: four platforms, four different years, same outcome. Users who left funds on an exchange lost access to them. Self-custody means your Bitcoin never sits on someone else's balance sheet. Hold your own keys.
flags: naming specific collapsed exchanges by name on an image is more visible than in a tweet, confirm this still clears the no-exchange-comparison rule even though the line is pre-approved

concepts.caption: The most common pushback we hear: "Bitcoin moves too much for me." Here's how dollar-cost averaging answers it: same small amount, same day, every week, regardless of price. No predictions, just consistency.
flags: review the reply wording before shipping to confirm it reads as mechanic explanation, not financial advice

concepts.caption: Relai never holds your Bitcoin. From the first purchase, it goes straight into your own self-custodial wallet. We hold zero user funds, by design. That's not a feature we added, it's the whole point of self-custody.

concepts.caption: Mt. Gox, 2014. QuadrigaCX, 2019. FTX, 2022. Celsius, 2022. All centralized. All collapsed. Every one of them held customer funds and lost them. Hold your own keys, hold your own Bitcoin.
